questions.q: Find the two angles between 0° and 180° for which sin x = 0.6. Give your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: sin x = sin(180° − x): the calculator only gives the acute angle.

questions.q:
Do not use a calculator in this question.
A triangle has two sides of length 6 cm and 10 cm. The angle between them is 150°.
You are given that sin 150° = ½.
Find the area of the triangle.
questions.tip: Area = ½ab sin C uses the angle between the two given sides.

questions.q:
In triangle ABC, AB = 12 cm, BC = 9.5 cm and angle ACB = 58°.
(a) Calculate angle BAC. [3]
(b) Find angle ABC. [1]
questions.tip: Pair each side with the angle opposite it: BC is opposite A, AB is opposite C.

questions.q:
A triangle has sides of length 9 cm, 13 cm and 17 cm.
(a) Calculate the largest angle of the triangle. [3]
(b) Calculate the area of the triangle. [2]
questions.model:
(a) The largest angle is opposite the longest side (17 cm).
cos θ = (81 + 169 − 289) ÷ (2 × 9 × 13) = −39 ÷ 234 = −0.1667
θ = 99.6°.
(b) Area = ½ × 9 × 13 × sin 99.59° = 57.7 cm².
questions.tip: A negative cosine means an obtuse angle; the calculator handles this automatically with cos⁻¹.

questions.q:
A ship sails from port P to point Q, 15 km on a bearing of 072°.
It then sails from Q to point R, 22 km on a bearing of 195°.
(a) Show that angle PQR = 57°. [2]
(b) Calculate the distance PR. [3]
(c) Calculate the bearing of R from P. [3]
ms: (a) M1: bearing of P from Q = 252° (072 + 180), or alternate angle 72° used with 195 − 180 = 15
(c) M1: sine rule or cosine rule for angle QPR, e.g. sin QPR = 22 sin 57° ÷ 18.70
questions.tip: Draw a north line at every point you use and mark the bearings on your sketch before calculating.

questions.q:
VABCD is a pyramid with a rectangular base ABCD. AB = 8 cm and BC = 6 cm.
The vertex V is vertically above M, the centre of the base. VA = VB = VC = VD = 13 cm.
(a) Calculate the height VM. [3]
(b) Calculate the angle between the edge VA and the base ABCD. [2]
(c) Calculate angle VBC. [2]
ms: (b) M1: tan θ = 12/5 or cos θ = 5/13 or sin θ = 12/13
(c) M1: cos VBC = 3/13 (triangle VBC is isosceles, half of BC = 3) or cosine rule
questions.model:
(a) AC = √(64 + 36) = 10 cm, so AM = 5 cm.
VM = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.
(b) The angle is VAM: tan VAM = 12 ÷ 5, so angle = 67.4°.
(c) Triangle VBC has VB = VC = 13 and BC = 6. The perpendicular from V bisects BC, so cos VBC = 3 ÷ 13.
Angle VBC = 76.7°.
questions.tip: The angle between a line and a plane is found in the right-angled triangle formed by the line, its projection on the plane and the vertical.
